newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-NORTHERN HEMISPHERE CATCHING UP, SAYS WHEELER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NORTHERN HEMISPHERE CATCHING UP, SAYS WHEELER.

text.p: Former England captain Peter Wheeler believes the gap in standards between northern and southern hemisphere rugby will soon be non-existent.

Helping to launch First Division Rugby (FDR), the latest organisation representing England's top professional clubs, Wheeler said the new money flowing into the European game was already paying dividends on the field.
"The top league clubs are bonded together, having committed 30 million pounds ($47.63 million) to the future development of grounds, facilities and players," said Wheeler.
"We must never be looking over our shoulder again, fearing a takeover by southern hemisphere media. If we develop, we will never be second best again to Australia and the rest."
England centre Damian Hopley used the occasion to call for an end to the power struggle between the clubs and the Rugby Football Union, currently locked in negiotiations over the game's future.
"We are hopeful of a resolution in due course," said a spokesman.
